recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not change Coverage.order to string for this issue; if Coverage.sequence is ever reintroduced, evaluate it against the original FHIR-12360 rationale for non-numeric sequence identifiers.
issue_request: FHIR-12360 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 Financial Management change request asking to change Coverage.dependent and Coverage.sequence from positiveInt to string so non-numeric values such as "03" could be represented.
initial_application: Historical commit 43806174288e821cb06173a72cde96317186412b included tracker 12360 and changed the Coverage spreadsheet source so Coverage.dependent and Coverage.sequence were typed as string, with corresponding dependent and sequence search parameters changed from number to string.
additional_context: Coverage is active in source/fhir.ini. Current Coverage source has Coverage.dependent and the Coverage-dependent search parameter as string. Current Coverage source has no Coverage.sequence element because the later Published/Persuasive FHIR-15564 decision accepted Coverage.class and removed Grouping and Sequence; FHIR-15564 is already represented on the combined branch by commit 1b6fcc57dc8ac6ca69ec4e5d651f9c57312c4093. Coverage.order is a separate positiveInt coordination-of-benefits ordering element introduced by FHIR-12231/FHIR-7863 and later clarified by FHIR-43028.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No active Coverage element remains incorrectly typed for FHIR-12360, and Coverage.order should not be retargeted by a sequence-typing issue.

related_jiras.note: Accepted the Coverage.class structure and removed Grouping and Sequence, explaining why Coverage.sequence is no longer present; it is already reconciled on the combined branch.
Added Coverage.order as a distinct positiveInt ordering element rather than changing the old Coverage.sequence element.
Clarified that Coverage.sequence was for renewal sequence numbers and added separate Coverage.order for coverage ordering.
Clarified Coverage.order and its relationship to Account.coverage.priority while retaining it as a separate element.
Earlier issue also required Coverage.dependent to support string values rather than positiveInt.
